budget.tuning_status: UNTUNED: these are the starting parameters named in the implementation prompt (AdamW, lr=3e-4, identical step count). No per-method hyper-parameter search was run.

candidate_reference.source: mechanism suite (trained checkpoint, not retrained in this comparison)

input_spec.notes: same 8-frame history as N01, recurrent hidden state of width 32 (RAFT-style ConvGRU); no correspondence, no support domains, no budget conditioning; state persists across encode calls until reset_state().

fixed time constant decay=0.9; recursive per frame, state persists across encode calls until reset_state(); no adaptation to noise, motion or budget; `variance` is accepted for interface parity but unused.
uniform causal average of the last 8 frames (window=max_history); no adaptation, no motion compensation; `variance` is accepted for interface parity but does not reweight evidence.

recursive noise-weighted estimate, K = V/(V+v) with the per-pixel supplied variance; explicit mean/var state, no process noise, no decay, no motion; state persists across encode calls until reset_state().

uniform causal average (8-frame budget) with integer/subpixel motion compensation using the shared CausalCorrespondence (alignment=fixed, so the same learnable residual gate as the candidate); one correspondence estimate per new frame; no support-domain merge/split, no selector, no budget conditioning.

N01 candidate: support-domain reorganisable multi-timescale integration (hysteretic merge/split support graph, analytic domain selector, time_depths=(1, 4, 8), budget_conditioning=False, max_updates=2); same causal correspondence and history length as the motion-compensated baseline.
ablation: time depth fixed at 8 frames and budget conditioning disabled; otherwise the same encoder, correspondence and history length as n01.

ablation: merge_threshold=0 with split_threshold=-1 keeps all one-hop edges permanently open (no hysteresis, no split, no occlusion release) under the analytic selector; otherwise the same encoder, correspondence and budget as n01.
C3 control: only the final (current) frame of the window is read; earlier frames are skipped, so there is no temporal integration. GroupNorm stem, no BatchNorm, no correspondence.

falsification.statement: On the narrow-tolerance, high-SNR slice the candidate must not trade fast thin-edge accuracy for static averaging: mean position error on 'fast' must exceed the mean on 'still' by more than 1.5 px.
falsification.threshold: delta(fast - still) > 1.5 px on the high/narrow slice

falsification.statement: The candidate must not degenerate into a maximum-window average: the effective history length must not sit within 5% of max_history, and the mean weighted support count must stay below the full (2r+1)^2 window mass.
falsification.threshold: history within 5% of max_history AND support_count >= 0.9 * window area

falsification.statement: The candidate must not be worse than the strongest static-history baseline (fixed average over the same history) on the fast+motion slice by more than 2 px.
The support graph must actually reorganise: either merge_count or split_count must be non-zero in the mechanism matrix, otherwise the hysteresis band is inert.
falsification.threshold: merge_count == 0 AND split_count == 0 on every condition

not_measured: closed-loop robot success rate (no robot or simulator in this run)
real camera RAW data (synthetic weak-edge task only)
hard real-time guarantees: --deadline_ms is an optional soft budget, not polled

units.budget: effective update count per step minus the declared target update count
units.latency_ms: milliseconds of wall time on this machine; the sample age (algorithmic lag) is reported separately and is never mixed into this number
units.location_heatmap: logits over the HxW measurement grid; cross-entropy target is a Gaussian heatmap with sigma in pixels
units.location_huber: pixel units: mean over the diagonal of |pred_xy - target_xy|
units.measurement_prediction: normalised measurement units (x=(raw-black)/(white-black)); target is the held-out pixel block of frame t-1, input replacement is a neighbourhood mean
units.position_error: pixels, row/col convention matching target_xy (normalised in [0,1])
